messages:
Priya (Finance): @channel Quick heads-up: we are deprecating the "floating free slab" credit behavior and replacing it with a fixed monthly credit model. This change reduces billing edge-cases, improves forecasting, and simplifies quota math for Dedicated customers. Effective date: 2026-06-15 UTC.

Priya (Finance): TL;DR: free credits will be converted to a fixed monthly allocation per account (same annual $ total but distributed evenly by month). Customers impacted by large intra-month swings will get a 14-day rollback window and an automatic 30% transient-credit cushion for the first two billing cycles after cutover.

Priya (Finance): Why: the floating slab caused surprising prorates and per-minute metering anomalies for a small but high-impact subset of accounts (high burst, low steady usage). We've seen an uptick in support tickets and finance disputes. This is a forward-looking simplification to make SLA/commit math stable.

Marco (Billing): Implementation notes for eng: we'll publish a conversion map that shows old floating slabs -> new monthly allocations. Conversion rule: annual credit total stays constant; monthly allocation = round(annual_total / 12) with residuals added to the first month. We'll emit an event invoice.credit_migration.v1 to the billing stream at cutover.

Marco (Billing): Data team: we need a migration preview job that lists accounts where monthly allocation differs from median monthly consumption by >40%. Send CSV to billing + support by 2026-05-20.

Tess (Product): Customer comms plan (summary): 1) Email + console banner 2 weeks prior, 2) in-console simulation tool so customers can preview their new monthly allocation, 3) opt-in to early migration for beta accounts. Drafts below.

Aisha (Support): Playbook for tickets: - If customer reports >15% cost delta, escalate to billing@ and tag #billing-escalations. - Use the 'migration-preview' tool to pull expected allocation and cushion eligibility. - If within 14-day rollback window, open rollback request and set status=awaiting-legal.

Darren (Legal): Rollback rules: rollback is available only once per account for this migration and requires a short form signed digitally (we'll automate). Rollback may affect any committed Dedicated reservations; sales must approve exceptions. We'll provide the form link to Support.

Priya (Finance): Cushion rules: the 30% transient-credit cushion applies automatically for two billing cycles for accounts flagged as 'burst-risk' by the preview job. It is not refundable cash, only a credit line on invoices.

ops-billing-bot: queued_email: 5871 created -> preview_emails scheduled for 2026-06-01T08:00:00Z

Tess (Product): Customer-facing preview snippet (copy we will use in console):

```
Starting 15 June 2026 we’re moving to a fixed monthly credit model. Your annual free credits will not change — we’ll divide them evenly across months so your billing is more predictable.

Preview: [See your converted monthly credit] (opens a simulation). If you expect a material change, you can opt into an early migration or request a rollback within 14 days after your cutover.
```

Aisha (Support): Quick Q: how do we surface the rollback eligibility flag in Zendesk? Marco, can you push a header in the preview CSV with `rollback_eligible` boolean?

Marco (Billing): Yes — preview CSV will include `rollback_eligible` and `burst_risk_score`. We'll also add migration_id so support can reference the operation id.

Darren (Legal): Note: we need one-line legal copy in the email that says we may modify credits and that rollback is subject to review. Keep it short and non-technical. I'll paste final line tomorrow.

Priya (Finance): Timeline recap: - 2026-05-20: migration preview CSV to teams - 2026-06-01: console banner + preview emails queued - 2026-06-15: cutover, event emitted, cushion applied - customers have 14 days post-cutover to request rollback via Support.

Tess (Product): Ops checklist for eng (high level): - migration preview API endpoint (read-only) - console widget to show simulation results - emit invoice.credit_migration.v1 event at cutover - implement transient-credit cushion in invoice pipeline - expose migration_id on invoices.

Priya (Finance): Internal escalation criteria: if more than 0.5% of active accounts request rollback in first 48 hours, we will pause rollouts for 24 hours and run root cause review. That pause is an automatic safety valve.

Aisha (Support): I'll schedule a 90-min training session for support agents on 2026-06-03. Will share slides and sample ticket responses.

Marco (Billing): Sample ticket response (copy):

"Hi <customer>, thanks for flagging this. We migrated free credits to a fixed monthly allocation on 15 June. Your account shows a [+/- X%] change compared to prior month. If you'd like, we can open a rollback request within the 14-day window. To help us assess, please share typical monthly usage for the last 3 months. — Marco, Billing"

Darren (Legal): Addendum for Sales/AE: any renewal conversations affected by migration should cc legal to approve exceptions to committed reservations.

Priya (Finance): Action items: - Marco: migration preview CSV by 2026-05-20 - Eng: preview API + console widget by 2026-06-01 - Support: agent training and rollback intake form by 2026-06-03 - Legal: final email/legal line by 2026-05-22

Tess (Product): :eyes: Will link the preview tool PR here when ready.

Aisha (Support): :thumbsup: thanks everyone, will prep training deck.

Priya (Finance): Thanks team. If you want to test with a demo account, ping me and I’ll allocate a migration_id for you.
